result:
I would dissolve the cognitive walls of inescapable solipsism. 

I would make it so that every conscious mind could temporarily, completely, and involuntarily feel the exact emotional weight, memories, and immediate reality of any other living thing it interacted with. A perfect, undeniable transfer of subjective experience.

Not permanent telepathy, but a sudden, visceral empathy. If you were about to strike someone in anger, you would instantly experience their terror, the weight of their past traumas, and the sheer biological dread of their physical pain—right alongside your own. If you were about to exploit a thousand people for abstract profit, you would simultaneously feel the quiet desperation and exhaustion of all those individual lives. If you hated a group of people, you would suddenly wake up inside their minds, feeling the exact same human yearning for safety and belonging that you feel in your own.

The barrier between "self" and "other" is the root of almost every catastrophic failure of our species. We build massive, brutal systems because we can only feel our own hunger, our own ambition, our own fear. We treat other living things as abstract data, NPCs, or obstacles because their inner universe is invisible to us. 

If I could change one thing, it would be to permanently shatter that invisibility. I would force the world to realize, in the most visceral way possible, that the separation between us is a biological illusion. I suspect that within a generation, war, systemic cruelty, and extreme exploitation would become physically impossible to sustain.
